Messages.Body:
curt...@aol.com (CurtAdams) writes:

>Mine say "any blocker must pay 1 blood to attempt to block this vampire".

>Now how does this affect allies?

>Read literally, they can't block - the have no blood, only life.

>Can they
>a) Not block
>b) Block by paying the appropriate number of life
>c) Block without penalty

>I favor c), on the grounds that Muddle wouldn't care WHAT some vampires
>rep in the Camarilla was. But this ain't what the cards say. Game
>balance would seem to favor a) as that card almost never sees use now.

I would favor c) as well. Game balance? You guys don't use Exemplary?
We put a few in our decks quite often (esp. in obfuscate decks). I think
it is a very worthwhile card already.

Shall I put you down for c) in the house rules list?

L. Scott

My group actually sees the Camarilla Exemplary fairly often. While we
haven't actually seen this situation (funny now that I think about it) I
would tend to think option b. The rules on Allies state that they should
be treated as vampires in most cases, except that they cannot renew their
life. So I would think that they would need to spend 1 life to attempt to
block. Perhaps the reason we have never seen this is that it is generally
easier to lose a blood of a vamp than to lose a life off an ally.

Just my opinion

stephen

12.3.1
Recruit Ally:
Allies are not spoken of as having blood points.

(allies) could care less for any social status a vampire has within the
Camarilla.

From a role-playing standpoint, the card is damn confusing. Why do you
take damage by blocking someone popular? The best answer is that because
you are screwing around with such a well-known and well-liked figure,
Archons, concerned parties, Prince's minions, etc... take it upon
themselves to slap you around a bit.
It makes more sense to maybe take the damage _after_ the block, ("you
got in a fight with who?") but game mechanics-wise I like the way it
works now.

Anyway, a Garou, street gang, Sabbat, etc... messing around with such
a well-respected guy is certainly subject, or even moreso, to this same
abuse by all these concerned parties.
Role-playing wise I vote for, ummm, b(?) Everyone loses a life/blood
counter.
